axes.label: Communication
axes.blurb: Say the true thing in the fewest words a stranger can act on.

axes.label: Comprehension
axes.blurb: Understand code you did not write before you touch it.

axes.label: Vision
axes.blurb: Choose what is worth building, and say why.

axes.label: Verification
axes.blurb: Prove it works. Especially when a model told you it does.

drills.title: The five questions before you code
drills.prompt: Give me a vague feature request the way a real stakeholder would say it. I will ask you questions until I could build it without guessing. Stop me when I start guessing. Then tell me which question I should have asked first, and why.
drills.done_when: You reached a buildable spec in under eight questions, and you know which one you missed.

drills.title: Context gathering under a budget
drills.prompt: I am about to change a codebase I do not know. Interview me about how I would find the three files that matter, with a hard budget of ten minutes of reading. Push back when my plan is really just grep-and-hope.
drills.done_when: You can name a repeatable method for finding the blast radius, not a lucky search.

drills.title: Taking initiative without going rogue
drills.prompt: Give me a situation where the ticket is wrong. Make me decide: do the ticket, push back, or do something adjacent. Then challenge my reasoning about who I would need to tell, and when.
drills.done_when: You made a call and named who you would tell before you did it.

drills.title: Defend a change against follow-ups
drills.prompt: I will describe a change I made. Act as a skeptical senior engineer in an interview. Ask me two levels of why on every claim. Call it out when I invent detail rather than saying I do not know.
drills.done_when: You survived two levels of why on every claim without inventing anything.

drills.title: Catch the model lying
drills.prompt: Write me a confident, plausible, and subtly wrong explanation of how a piece of code works. Do not tell me where the error is. Then grade how I found it, and what check I should have run first.
drills.done_when: You found the error with a check, not a hunch, and wrote the check down.

drills.title: Take a hard review well
drills.prompt: Review a change I describe as a blunt maintainer. Include one comment that is simply wrong. Grade how I respond to all of them, especially the wrong one.
drills.done_when: You disagreed with the wrong comment without getting defensive, and changed the rest.

drills.title: Turn work into a story with receipts
drills.prompt: I will paste a link and a description of something I built. Interrogate me until there is a two-minute story with a real obstacle in it. Reject anything a person who only prompted a model could also claim.
drills.done_when: The story survived the 'a vibe-coder could claim this' test.

handoff.title: The FOR ADEN block
handoff.instruction: End every session by asking the Coach for this, then paste it into #asks. It is how I review your thinking without sitting through the session.
handoff.template:
FOR ADEN
Drill: <which one>
Where I got stuck:
What I would do differently:
What I still cannot defend:
Claims I called sure that I could not show: <count and one example>
My prompts worth reviewing: <paste 1-2>
